::: {.course-numbers-page}
MBA 693R · STRAT 490R
:::

The **BYU AI Foundry** is a sponsored-project studio inside the BYU Marriott School of
Business. Client organizations bring a real, open-ended business problem. A small team of
high-performing students, guided by faculty, spends an academic year designing, prototyping,
and testing an AI-enabled solution to it.

The Foundry is not an internship placement and not a research project. It is delivery work.
Every engagement ends with something the client can use: a working prototype, a decision
framework with the rules written down, a model whose outputs can be explained, and a
recommendation the client's leadership can act on.

Students typically complete
[MSB 341 - Product Management](https://byu-strategy.github.io/product-management/)
before joining a Foundry team, so they arrive with product and applied AI skills already built.

## Course Numbers

This course is cross-listed under two course numbers. It is all the same class: everyone meets
together Fridays 8:00 to 11:50 AM in 2140 TNRB, works on the same client teams, uses this site,
and is graded on the same rubric. Register under whichever number fits your program.

| Course | Section | Title | Credit Hours |
|--------|---------|-------|--------------|
| MBA 693R | 011 | Special Topics in Management | 3.0 |
| STRAT 490R | 001 | Topics in Strategic Management | 3.0 |

Mixed MBA and undergraduate teams are intentional. Client engagements benefit from the range,
and it mirrors how real delivery teams are staffed.

## Program At a Glance

| | |
|---|---|
| **Duration** | 8 months (2 semesters) |
| **Period** | September 2, 2026 – April 14, 2027 |
| **Team size** | 4–6 students per project |
| **Student hours** | 8–12 hours per week, per student |
| **Client commitment** | ~1 hour per week |
| **Sponsorship** | $22,000 per project |
| **Location** | Remote, with optional on-site visits |
| **IP** | Sponsor retains all deliverables and IP |

## What Makes This Different from an Engineering Capstone

The BYU engineering capstones build physical and embedded systems: CAD, prototypes, PCBs,
firmware, security assessments. The AI Foundry builds **business decision systems**: strategy
frameworks, prioritization and scoring models, forecasting and predictive analytics, financial
models, and the software that makes those things usable by a decision maker.

If the question is "how do we build this thing," that is engineering. If the question is
"which things should we build, in what order, and how do we know," that is the Foundry.
